ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the charge of S$21.10 stands and the disputed S$2.00 is not refunded.

Distance test (POL-RD-01). The platform's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-02806) measures the trip at 14.84 km; the booked optimal route (EV-TRIP-02806) is 14.0 km. I have used the trace figure of 14.84 km, as POL-RD-01 requires, and not the rounded 14.8 km convenience copy on the trip record. The excess is 0.84 km, which is 6.00% of the optimal distance. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only when the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, and both tests must pass. The 0.84 km does clear the 0.8 km absolute gate by 0.04 km, but 6.00% is far below the 20% gate, so the establishment test fails and no route deviation exists on this trip. Both advocates reached this same conclusion and I accept it.

Trace integrity (POL-RD-07). The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 117 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gap longer than 90 seconds and a maximum gap of 0.0 s. It is also COMPLETE at weight 1.0 in the pre-pass. The trace therefore governs the threshold test at full weight, and no impairment escalation arises.

Traffic excuse and the missing advisory (POL-RD-13). The driver's statement that he followed the navigation was not tested against a traffic advisory, because the only advisory in the bundle (EV-ADVIS-02806-01) is MISSING at weight 0.0 with no payload. POL-RD-13 provides that a traffic cause asserted for a measured deviation cannot be run without an advisory on file, and any such assertion carries no weight; but no deviation was measured here, so this changes nothing. The two discarded claims that cited the missing advisory are recorded in the audit below and were discarded by the referee for not naming its issue code.

Billing integrity (POL-RD-09). The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02806) reconciles to a charged total of 21.10, with zero ERP gantries, zero tolls, zero airport surcharge and a surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare breakdown. No phantom line or wrongly applied surcharge appears, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to correct and no billing-integrity referral is produced.

Profiles (POL-GEN-01). Both profiles are context only and none of their citable counters helps either side: the rider's deviation_claims_60d is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration test is not triggered; the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 of 230 completed trips, so the POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation pattern (and its conduct referral) is not available. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 names and was correctly not substituted.

Outcome. With no deviation established, the rider's claim that the fare was higher than normal is not made out on the money side either: the optimal-route recomputation would be 20.3920 against 21.10, but POL-RD-02 never runs because POL-RD-01 fails. Under POL-GEN-03 the result is NO_ACTION: fare_breakdown.payment_status stays CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd stays 0.0. There is no monetary effect, so no execution-threshold question arises. The rider may appeal this provisional ruling once under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
